translationRepairs: Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for arranging annals by year but writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.
Yingshi especially faulted Master Zichang for not compiling year-by-year annals and writing biographical accounts instead, which later generations followed—this was not canonical teaching.
不編年而為列傳 means Zichang did not compile year-by-year annals but wrote biographies; the before text reverses the negation into arranging annals by year.
After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only those who had received instruction in Qi.
After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, he recorded only what could instruct and regulate the living.
訓齊生人 is the verb compound “instruct and regulate the living,” not “instruction in Qi”; the before invents the polity name 齊.
After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only those who received the instruction of Qi were recorded.
After the three schools of the Spring and Autumn, only what instructed and regulated the living was recorded.
Same error as the idiomatic field: 訓齊生人 means what instructs and regulates the living, not “the instruction of Qi.”
Zheng and Ming were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
Zheng and E were most renowned; Tan and Shi passed their fame down through literature.
Authoritative witnesses read 拯與崿名最著: the pair is Zheng and Li E (崿/㟧), not “Ming” from bare 名 and not Chui (垂). The chapter dossier omits 崿; Chui belongs to the earlier roster, not this summary.
Gao Shi recommended him for trial appointment as judge of the Grand Court and as investigation commissioner of Huainan.
Gao Shi recommended him for trial appointment as judge of the Grand Court and as administrative assistant to the investigation commissioner of Huainan.
淮南采訪判官 is administrative assistant/judge (判官) under the investigation commissioner, not the commissioner (采訪使) himself.
Gao Shi memorialized to try him as Judge of the Grand Court and as Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
Gao Shi memorialized to try him as Judge of the Grand Court and as Administrative Assistant to the Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
Same office error: 判官 is not 采訪使; the trial appointment is as Huainan investigation assistant.
Yan Zhenqing, military governor of Zhexi, recommended him as marching sima; he was summoned as attendant of the heir apparent but firmly declined.
Yan Zhenqing, military governor of Zhexi, recommended him as marching sima; he was summoned as Imperial Diarist but firmly declined.
起居舍人 is Imperial Diarist; attendant of the heir apparent would be 太子舍人, a different office.
Yan Zhenqing, Military Governor of Zhexi, memorialized him as Marching Sima; he was summoned as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but firmly declined.
Yan Zhenqing, Military Governor of Zhexi, memorialized him as Marching Sima; he was summoned as Imperial Diarist, but firmly declined.
Same mistranslation: 起居舍人 is Imperial Diarist, not Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and went weeping; an edict enfeoffed him as Vice Director of the Palace Library.
He died at forty-six; Hui and the others wore mourning and went weeping; an edict posthumously appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Library.
詔贈 is a posthumous appointment/grant, not enfeoffment.
A palace envoy passed through the province and demanded bribes without end; Wang Sui, magistrate of Nanchang, wished to prosecute him and sought Gao's counsel.
A palace envoy passed through the province and demanded bribes without end; Wang Gou, magistrate of Nanchang, wished to prosecute him and sought Gao's counsel.
王遘 is Wang Gou (Gòu); Sui misromanizes 遘.
A palace envoy passed through the province and sought gain without limit; Magistrate Wang Sui of Nanchang wished to prosecute him and consulted with Gao.
A palace envoy passed through the province and sought gain without limit; Magistrate Wang Gou of Nanchang wished to prosecute him and consulted with Gao.
Same romanization fix: 遘 is Gou, not Sui.
Sui understood and thanked him profusely.
Gou understood and thanked him profusely.
Short form 遘 must be Gou to match the personal name.
Sui understood, and thanked him lavishly.
Gou understood, and thanked him lavishly.
Same short-name fix: 遘 is Gou.
When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If you still will not rise, cut off your head and bring it to me."
When Lushan rebelled he sent Cai Xide with a sealed blade to summon him, saying: "If he still will not rise, cut off his head and bring it to me."
Lushan’s order to Cai about Ji uses 斷其頭 (his head) and third-person 即不起; second-person “your head” invents address to Ji.
when the harvest was abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor and narrow-minded in the village.
when the harvest was abundant he distributed the surplus among the poor and straitened in the village.
貧狹 means the poor and hard-pressed, not “narrow-minded”; the before invents a moral judgment absent from the Chinese.
Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had defiled officials bow in ranks to shame his heart.
Emperor Suzong ordered him lodged in the offices of the Three Departments and had defiled officials bow in ranks to shame their hearts.
以愧其心 follows 使汙賊官羅拜: 其 refers to the defiled officials’ hearts, not Ji’s.
Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer for Xiangyang in Shanxi, and he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
Lai Tian recruited him as staff officer for Xiangyang in Shaanxi, and he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
陜西 is the Tang Shaanxi circuit (west of the passes), not Shanxi (山西).
The next day twenty who came to Cheng to return home to care for parents; those who had not attended parents for three years he expelled.
The next day twenty came to Cheng to return home and care for their parents; those who had not attended their parents for three years he expelled.
謁城還養者二十輩 needs a finite verb; the before is an ungrammatical fragment, and the repair matches the Chinese and the idiomatic.
At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;
At the gates of Yu Fu and Bian Que they did not reject the sick;
俞、扁 is the classical physician pair Yu Fu (俞跗) then Bian Que (扁鵲); Chunyu Yi misidentifies 俞 and reverses the order.
At the gates of Bian Que and Chunyu Yi they did not reject the sick;
At the gates of Yu Fu and Bian Que they did not reject the sick;
Same identification: 俞、扁 are Yu Fu and Bian Que in that order, not Bian Que and Chunyu Yi.
Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern; hearing that your office is sending Master Yang back south.
Fortunate to live in an age without taboo, I cannot set forth the larger pattern, nor inform your office, regarding Master Yang's being sent back south.
不能論列大體，聞下執事 pairs “set forth the larger pattern” with “inform your office” about 還陽公之南; the before is a fragment and misreads 聞 as mere hearing.
The prefecture produced dwarfs who were sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from their lives and had nowhere to advance.
The prefecture produced dwarfs who were sent yearly as tribute to court; Cheng grieved that they were torn from home by separation, and he presented none.
生離 is living separation from home, and 無所進 means Cheng presented no dwarf tribute, not that the dwarfs had nowhere to advance.
At first, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them and they would not listen, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.
At first, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the students were about to follow the rebellion; Fan sternly rebuked them until they desisted, so none of the six halls' scholars were defiled.
With 故六館士無受汙者, 叱不聽 means Fan’s rebuke stopped them; “they would not listen” reverses the outcome.

When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent to aid the ruined royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.

When the court moved to Luoyang, Liu Can, hoping to please the wicked ministers, slaughtered the empire's talent to help destroy the royal house; an edict summoned Tu to court; Tu pretended to drop his tablet and affected the manner of a rustic old man.
助喪王室 means helping bring about the ruin of the royal house; “aid the ruined royal house” misreads 喪 as an adjective.

He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once xiu, beauty is complete.

He built a plain pavilion and lodge, painting all the Tang's men of integrity and literary men; he named the pavilion Xiuxiu and wrote a text to show his aim: "Xiu means beautiful; once at rest, beauty is complete.
After defining 休 as “beautiful,” 既休而美具 uses 休 as “at rest”; leaving it as untranslated “xiu” under-translates the verb.
Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true husbands indeed!
Dexiu by virtue, Cheng by blunt integrity, Tu by knowing fate—their aims contended with autumn frost in severity; true men indeed!
丈夫 here praises upright men of character, not husbands; the idiomatic “true men” is the right sense.
